provenance: SYNTHETIC — modeled full-service restaurant load, not a Green Button export and not any real customer.
syntheticNotes:
Generated by a one-off script (packages/rating-engine/gen-restaurant.mjs, not committed) to model a small full-service restaurant in SCE territory across calendar year 2026, 15-minute resolution, 35040 readings.

ALGORITHM: for each 15-minute local interval, kWh = BASE_KW x hourlyMultiplier[hour] x dayOfWeekMultiplier[weekday] x seasonalFactor(month, hour) x dayNoise x intervalNoise x 0.25 (kW-average to kWh).

ASSUMPTIONS, ALL FABRICATED (not from any real restaurant's data or any published EIA/utility load-shape study — chosen to be directionally realistic, not to match a specific source):
- BASE_KW = 18: overnight baseline (walk-ins, freezers, security lighting, HVAC setback).
- Hourly shape: low overnight, ramping through the morning, a lunch peak near noon (~3x baseline), an afternoon lull, then a dinner-service peak from roughly 4-9pm reaching ~4.2x baseline — deliberately the largest draw of the day, and deliberately overlapping SCE's summer on-peak window (4-9pm) and the winter mid-peak window, since that overlap is the exact product question this fixture exists to exercise.
- Day-of-week: Mon-Wed flat, Thu/Fri/Sat progressively busier (up to 1.20x), Sun 1.05x — applied as a single scalar over the whole day's shape. A real restaurant's Sunday likely shifts toward brunch and away from dinner rather than just scaling uniformly; not modeled, flagged here rather than silently assumed.
- Seasonal: a 1.28x multiplier on summer (Jun-Sep) hours 11am-8pm (AC load), a smaller 1.08x on summer hours outside that window (refrigeration working harder, some overnight AC cycling), no seasonal adjustment in winter (assumes gas heat, common in CA restaurants, not electric).
- Random variation: a fresh +/-10% multiplier drawn once per calendar day (busier/quieter days), plus an independent +/-5% multiplier per interval, both from a seeded mulberry32 PRNG (seed 20260101) so this file is exactly reproducible from the generator script, not from Math.random().

RESULT: 361567 kWh over the year, average 41.3 kW, peak 15-minute-average demand 128.7 kW (comfortably within TOU-GS-2's 20-200 kW band; the peak is well short of 200 kW even under this generator's worst-case combination of a busy summer Saturday dinner rush plus maximum random noise, so eligibility for TOU-GS-2 itself is not in question for this profile).

KNOWN LIMITATION A REAL BILL COULD CATCH THAT THIS FILE CANNOT: this profile is generated NATIVELY at 15-minute resolution, so every reading already IS the 15-minute average — there is no finer-grained spike this file could ever reveal being smoothed out by demand-window averaging. A real restaurant's actual sub-15-minute equipment cycling (walk-in compressor and defrost cycles, HVAC compressor starts, multiple ovens igniting near-simultaneously at the start of dinner service) could produce brief spikes well above what a 15-minute average shows, meaning a REAL Green Button export (especially any 5-minute-interval data) could report a materially higher facilities-demand peak than this file ever will. This fixture cannot be used to validate that the engine's demand-window averaging matches SCE's own metering in practice — only a real interval export can do that.
